mainTopic: Laws of the כהן גדול: exile, being judged, testifying, the courts he may not sit on, and חליצה.
overview: This amud keeps working through the laws of the כהן גדול. First a פסוק shows that a כהן גדול who kills by accident goes to an עיר מקלט, even though he can never leave. If he sins, he is judged like a הדיוט, and he needs a court of seventy-one only for a truly 'great matter'. Next the גמרא asks how he can be required to testify, since an honored person may skip a מצוה that is beneath his dignity. After several tries, it explains that he testifies in front of the king, who leaves before the judges deliberate. The גמרא then explains why a king may not sit on the סנהדרין, and why neither a king nor a כהן גדול may sit on the court that adds a month to the year. רב פפא learns from this that the weather follows the months. A story about three cattle herders seems to show the opposite, but the גמרא answers that the חכמים relied on their own calculations. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that a כהן גדול does חליצה and never יבום, and begins a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא had to say a כהן גדול is exiled
steps.stepSummary: Since a כהן גדול who killed can never leave the עיר מקלט, we might think he is not exiled at all, so the ברייתא tells us he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a rule that someone who kills a כהן גדול, or a כהן גדול who killed someone, never leaves the city of refuge. So I might think a כהן גדול is not exiled at all. That is why the ברייתא had to teach us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why the ברייתא needed to say that a כהן גדול goes to גלות. Without it, we might have thought he is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an accidental killer leaves the עיר מקלט when the כהן גדול dies. When a כהן גדול is the killer or the victim, there is no way out, and he stays there forever. One could reason that if exile would be endless, it should not apply to him at all. The ברייתא rules out that thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him be exiled (to an עיר מקלט)
It comes to teach us (this is the new point)

phrases.english: One who kills a High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָרַג אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ –
phrases.english: or a High Priest who killed a person –
never leaves there;
so I might say he is not exiled at all –
so it teaches us that he is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לָא לִיגְלֵי – קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an earlier question on the daf about why the ברייתא needed to say a כהן גדול goes to גלות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a possible mistaken thought (הוה אמינא) that the ברייתא comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a כהן גדול can never leave the עיר מקלט, he is not exiled at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is exiled, just like any other accidental killer.

steps.title: Maybe he really is not exiled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we should not accept that mistaken thought as the real law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say that is really the law, and he is not exiled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The reasoning that a כהן גדול is exempt sounded logical, so maybe it is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'mistaken thought' was not obviously wrong. If exile can never end for him, exempting him seems fair. The גמרא wants a source that forces him to go.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say it really is so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הוה אמינא from step 1 as possibly being the real law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a כהן גדול is exiled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The logic for exempting him seems strong, since his exile would never end.

steps.title: The word 'every' includes the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'every killer may flee there', and 'every' includes even a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'so that every killer may flee there.' Even a כהן גדול is included in this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The word 'every' (כל) includes the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone might exempt him, but the תורה's wording covers all killers with no exception. So the פסוק overrides the reasoning, and a כהן גדול must go to גלות.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול who kills by accident goes to גלות, because the פסוק says 'every killer'.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"That every killer may flee there" –
even a High Priest is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק that includes the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן גדול might be exempt from גלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'every' (כל) includes him, so he is exiled.

steps.title: Must a כהן גדול sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's words 'he transgresses an עשה and a לא תעשה' and asks whether that means he has to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: 'he transgresses a positive command and a prohibition.' Is it impossible for him not to sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא. It questions the odd wording, which sounds as if the כהן גדול always sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עובר על עשה ועל לא תעשה' read like a plain statement of fact. That would mean every כהן גדול sins. The גמרא points out that this cannot be what is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command (a מצוה to do something)
A prohibition (a מצוה not to do something)
Is it not possible without…? (must it be that…?)

phrases.aramaic: עוֹבֵר עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: "He transgresses a positive command and a prohibition."
Is it impossible that he not transgress?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts discussing a new line of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: As written, it sounds as if a כהן גדול always sins, which makes no sense.

steps.title: It means: if he sins, he is like a הדיוט
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that if a כהן גדול sins, he is treated like an ordinary person.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if he transgressed a positive command and a prohibition, he is like an ordinary person in all his matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as an 'if' sentence. If he sins, his status does not protect him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying he must sin. It is saying what happens if he does. He is judged and punished like any הדיוט.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִם עָבַר עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: if he transgressed a positive command and a prohibition,
he is like an ordinary person in all his matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by rereading the ברייתא as a conditional statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says a כהן גדול always sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means 'if he sins, he is like a הדיוט'.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say that a sinning כהן גדול is like anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need this rule at all. Of course a כהן גדול who sins is treated like anyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not supposed to state the obvious. So the גמרא looks for the new point hidden in the rule that he is like a הדיוט.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the rule explained in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a sinning כהן גדול is like a הדיוט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason to think otherwise, so the rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought every case needs seventy-one judges
steps.stepSummary: Since a כהן גדול is judged by a court of seventy-one, and רב אדא בר אהבה explains that as 'the matters of a great person', we might think all his cases need seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought otherwise. We learned in the משנה that a tribe, a false prophet, and a כהן גדול are judged only by a court of seventy-one. And רב אדא בר אהבה said that the פסוק 'every great matter they shall bring to you' means the matters of a great person. So I might think all the matters of a great person go to the seventy-one. The ברייתא teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows what is new in the ברייתא. Without it, we might think even small cases of a כהן גדול need the סנהדרין גדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (on daf 2a) says a כהן גדול is judged by seventy-one. רב אדא בר אהבה links this to the פסוק about a 'great matter', reading it as the matters of a great person. From that reading one could think every case of his goes to seventy-one. The ברייתא says he is like a הדיוט in ordinary cases, so a smaller court can judge him.

keyTerms.meaning: It could have entered your mind to say
A court of seventy-one (the סנהדרין גדולה)
The matters (cases) of a great person

steps.confusionAlert: The new point is not about whether he is punished. It is about which court judges him in ordinary cases.

phrases.english: It could have entered your mind to say,
since we learned:
They do not judge a tribe,
nor a false prophet,
nor a High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one,
and Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
"Every great matter they shall bring to you" –
means the matters of a great person,
phrases.notes: The 'great person' here is the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: so I might say all the matters of a great person go to seventy-one,
so it teaches us that they do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 6 by giving a reasonable mistaken thought.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a possible mistaken thought (הוה אמינא) that the ברייתא comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case of a כהן גדול, even a minor one, needs a court of seventy-one.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ordinary cases he is like a הדיוט and is judged by a regular court.

steps.title: Maybe all his cases do need seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why that mistaken thought should not be the real law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it really is so, that all his cases need seventy-one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. רב אדא בר אהבה's reading seemed to support sending all his cases to seventy-one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is about the matters of a great person, then maybe every case of his really does belong to the סנהדרין גדולה. The גמרא needs to show why that reading is too broad.

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that ordinary cases of a כהן גדול go to a regular court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אדא בר אהבה's reading of the פסוק seems to cover all his matters.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'the great matter', not 'the matters of a great person'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of a truly great matter, a capital case, so only those cases need seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'the matters of a great person'? It is written 'the great matter', meaning a matter that is truly great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the exact wording of the פסוק. Only a truly great matter, a capital case, needs a court of seventy-one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say 'דברי גדול' (matters of a great person). It says 'הדבר הגדול' (the great matter). So the case itself must be serious. A minor case of a כהן גדול is not a 'great matter', and he is judged like a הדיוט.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול needs a court of seventy-one only for a truly 'great matter', a capital case. In other cases he is judged like a הדיוט.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the limit on the special court for a כהן גדול: the seriousness of the case decides, not just his high position.

phrases.english: Is it written 'the matters of a great person'?
"The great matter" is written,
meaning a matter that is truly great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by reading the exact words of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the exact wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All matters of a כהן גדול go to seventy-one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a truly great matter (a capital case) goes to seventy-one.

steps.title: The משנה: a כהן גדול testifies and is testified about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה: a כהן גדול gives testimony, and others may testify about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the כהן גדול testifies, and people testify about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה about the כהן גדול. It is quoting this line to set up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the sugya discussed the כהן גדול being judged like anyone else. Now it turns to a different rule: he can be a witness and can be testified against. Quoting the line prepares the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: He testifies and they testify about him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the judging of a כהן גדול to his role as a witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול serves as a witness, and witnesses may testify about him.

steps.title: Challenge: an honored person may ignore a מצוה beneath his dignity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a כהן גדול can be required to testify. A ברייתא teaches that an honored person, like a זקן, may ignore a lost item when returning it is beneath his dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really testify? A ברייתא learns from the word 'and you shall ignore' that sometimes you may ignore a lost item and sometimes you may not. When may you? A כהן when the item is in a cemetery, a זקן when handling it is beneath his honor, or someone whose own work is worth more than the lost item. For these cases the תורה wrote 'and you shall ignore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that a כהן גדול testifies. It brings a ברייתא showing that the תורה lets an honored person skip a מצוה when doing it would lower his dignity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that a זקן may skip השבת אבידה when it is beneath his dignity. A כהן גדול has even greater honor. So perhaps he too should not be required to come and testify, and the משנה's rule seems difficult.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall ignore': the word from the פסוק about lost items
An elder or Torah scholar who deserves honor

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about returning lost items, not about testimony. The גמרא borrows its principle (an honored person may skip a מצוה beneath his dignity) and applies it to the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: He testifies?
But isn't it taught: "And you shall ignore" –
phrases.notes: דברים 22:1, the פסוק about returning your fellow's lost ox or sheep.

phrases.english: there are times that you ignore,
and there are times that you do not ignore.
How so?
A כהן, and it is in the cemetery,
phrases.notes: A כהן is not allowed to go into a cemetery, so he can't go in to get the item.

phrases.english: an elder, and it is not fitting for his dignity,
or if his own work
was worth more than his fellow's –
for this it says "and you shall ignore."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a כהן גדול testifies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a זקן may skip a מצוה beneath his dignity, a כהן גדול should be allowed to skip testifying for the sake of his honor.

steps.title: רב יוסף: he testifies only for the king
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the כהן גדול testifies only in a matter of the king, where his dignity is not lowered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: he testifies for the king.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף limits the משנה. The כהן גדול does not testify in every case, only in one connected to the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף accepts the challenge's principle that the כהן גדול need not lower himself. He reads the משנה's 'he testifies' as applying only to a king's matter, which suits his honor. The following steps work out exactly what 'for the king' means.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the challenge

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
He testifies for the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing when the כהן גדול testifies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן גדול testifies in any case, even below his honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: He testifies only in a king-related setting that fits his honor.

steps.title: But a king is not judged or testified about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה itself says a king does not judge, is not judged, does not testify, and is not testified about.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: the king does not judge and is not judged, does not testify and they do not testify about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the simple reading of רב יוסף, that the כהן גדול testifies in the king's own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one testifies about a king, then a king's case never comes to court. So the כהן גדול cannot be testifying in it, and רב יוסף's words need a different meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
He does not judge and is not judged

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
he does not judge and they do not judge him,
he does not testify and they do not testify about him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: לֹא דָּן וְלֹא דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב יוסף as 'he testifies in the king's case.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says no one testifies about a king, so there is no king's case to testify in.

steps.title: רבי זירא: he testifies for a king's son
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains רב יוסף to mean that the כהן גדול testifies in the case of a king's son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: he testifies for a king's son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא offers a new reading of רב יוסף's words. 'For the king' means for the king's son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king's son can be judged and testified about, so the problem from the משנה falls away. The idea is that testifying for someone of royal family would still suit the כהן גדול's honor.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reinterprets רב יוסף

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
He testifies for a king's son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of רב יוסף.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'For the king' means in the king's own case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'For the king' means for the king's son.

steps.title: But a king's son is an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי זירא: a king's son has no special status, so testifying for him would still be beneath the כהן גדול's dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: A king's son is an ordinary person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי זירא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הלכה a king's son is a הדיוט, just like anyone else. So testifying for him is no more honorable than testifying for any ordinary person, and the original challenge comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person with no special status

phrases.english: A king's son is an ordinary person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's reading 'for a king's son.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king's son has no special honor, so the כהן גדול's dignity would still be lowered.

steps.title: Rather: he testifies in front of the king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reading: the כהן גדול testifies only when the king is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he testifies in front of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third meaning of 'for the king.' It is not about whose case it is, but about who is sitting there when he testifies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case can be about anyone. The כהן גדול's honor is kept because he gives his testimony before the king rather than before ordinary judges alone.

phrases.english: Rather, he testifies in front of the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading after רבי זירא's was rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'For the king' refers to the person whose case it is.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'For the king' means the testimony is given in the king's presence.

steps.title: But a king may not sit on the סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a king is never seated on the סנהדרין, so how can testimony be given before him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we do not seat a king on the סנהדרין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a king may not sit among the judges, it seems the court could never hear testimony in his presence. This puts the third reading in doubt.

phrases.english: But we do not seat a king on the Sanhedrin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'in front of the king' reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the כהן גדול testifies before the king.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king is not allowed to sit on the סנהדרין, so he cannot be present in court.

steps.title: The king comes only to hear the testimony, then leaves
steps.stepSummary: For the honor of the כהן גדול the king comes and sits while the testimony is received. Then he gets up and leaves, and the judges discuss the case without him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the honor of the כהן גדול, the king comes and sits. They receive the testimony, the king gets up and leaves, and then we judges look into the case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the king is present only while the testimony is being heard. He leaves before the actual judging begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against seating a king on the סנהדרין is about him taking part in judging and deliberating. Here he only attends the testimony, out of respect for the כהן גדול, and is gone before the deliberation. This keeps both rules and settles how a כהן גדול can testify without losing his honor.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול does testify, but out of respect for him it is done in front of the king. The king hears the testimony and leaves before the judges deliberate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא balances a person's honor against his duty. The duty to testify stays in place, and the court arranges it so his dignity is protected.

phrases.english: Because of the honor of the High Priest
he comes and sits.
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the king, who comes to court just for this.

phrases.english: They receive his testimony,
he gets up and goes,
and we look into the case.
phrases.notes: The judges talk it over only after the king has left, so he never actually sits as a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם יְקָרָא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל אֲתָא וְיָתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about a king sitting on the סנהדרין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Testifying before the king would mean the king sits as a judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The king is present only for the testimony and leaves before deliberation.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא about the king and the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the ברייתא itself: a king is not seated on the סנהדרין, and neither a king nor a כהן גדול sits on the court for עיבור שנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself: We do not seat a king on the סנהדרין, and we do not seat a king or a כהן גדול on the court that adds a month to the year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the full text of a ברייתא it mentioned earlier, so it can explain it. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used this ברייתא only to show that a king does not sit on the סנהדרין. Now it studies the ברייתא on its own terms. The ברייתא has two rules, and the next steps give the reason for each.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': the גמרא returns to examine a source it quoted earlier
Making the year a leap year by adding a month

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא the גמרא leaned on in steps 17–18, when it said a king never sits on the סנהדרין.

phrases.english: We do not seat a king on the Sanhedrin,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מֶלֶךְ וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּעִיבּוּר שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: nor a king or a High Priest on the court for adding a month to the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא quoted in step 17 in order to explain it in full
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king may not sit on the סנהדרין, and neither a king nor a כהן גדול may sit on the court for עיבור שנה.

steps.title: The source for keeping a king off the סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The rule comes from the פסוק 'לא תענה על ריב', read as 'do not answer against a great person'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why no king on the סנהדרין? Because it says 'Do not answer in a dispute (ריב)', which is read as 'Do not answer against a great person (רב)'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the first rule, that a king may not sit on the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ריב is read as רב, a great person. A judge must not be put in a position where he has to argue against someone so powerful. If a king sat on the court, the other judges would be afraid to disagree with him.

phrases.english: A king on the Sanhedrin –
as it is written: "Do not answer in a dispute" –
do not answer against a great person.
phrases.notes: The word רִב is written without a yud, so it can also be read רַב, a great person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the first half of the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: A king may not be seated on the סנהדרין
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 23:2, 'לא תענה על ריב', read as 'על רב'

steps.title: Why the king and the כהן גדול are kept off עיבור שנה
steps.stepSummary: The king has a stake because of his soldiers' provisions, and the כהן גדול because of the cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Neither a king nor a כהן גדול sits on the court that adds a month. The king is kept off because of what he must provide for his soldiers. The כהן גדול is kept off because of the cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the second rule of the ברייתא and gives a reason for each person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of them would want the court not to add a month. A longer year means the king must pay and feed his army for longer. For the כהן גדול, an added month pushes יום כיפור later into colder weather, so a biased judge cannot sit.
steps.confusionAlert: The king is not suspected of bad character. The point is that he and the כהן גדול each have a personal interest in the decision, so they cannot judge it.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מֶלֶךְ וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּעִיבּוּר שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: Nor a king or a High Priest on the court for adding a month to the year.
A king – because of soldiers' provisions,
phrases.notes: An extra month means more months of food and pay for his army, so he would lean against adding it.

phrases.english: A High Priest – because of the cold.
phrases.notes: On יום כיפור he immerses again and again, so he would rather the day not fall later in the colder season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the ברייתא after step 20 explained the first
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king and the כהן גדול are kept off עיבור שנה because each has a personal interest against adding a month.

steps.title: רב פפא: the year follows the months
steps.stepSummary: From the כהן גדול's reason, רב פפא concludes that the weather follows the months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that the year goes by the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a general conclusion from the reason just given for the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול would only fear the cold if moving the calendar a month later also moved the weather. So the seasons must line up with the months as they are counted. If a month is added, the new תשרי will feel like a normal מרחשון.

keyTerms.meaning: The year (here, its seasons and weather)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Learn from this
the year follows the month.
phrases.notes: He means the weather goes by the month: push תשרי later and it gets colder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a general inference from the reason given in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seasons follow the counted months, so adding a month shifts the weather of each month.

steps.title: Challenge from the three cattle herders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב פפא and brings up three cattle herders whose words the חכמים overheard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But there were three cattle herders standing around, and the חכמים heard them say the following:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge רב פפא. This line sets up the story, and the herders' actual words come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אִינִי signals doubt about רב פפא's claim. The story will show that the חכמים decided on adding a month by looking at the actual season. That suggests the months follow the seasons, not the other way around.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But there were those three cattle herders
who were standing around,
and the Sages heard them saying:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an attack on רב פפא's inference in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the year follows the months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים set the calendar by checking the real season, which implies the months are adjusted to the seasons rather than the seasons following the months.

steps.title: The herders' signs of אדר and the added month
steps.stepSummary: Each herder gave a sign for knowing it is truly אדר. Since the signs had not come yet, the חכמים added a month that year.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: If the early and late crops sprout together, it is אדר; if not, it is not אדר. One said: If an ox can freeze to death in the snow in the morning and lie in a fig tree's shade at midday rubbing off its skin, it is אדר; if not, it is not אדר. One said: If a strong east wind blows and your warm breath overpowers it, it is אדר; if not, it is not אדר. And the חכמים added a month to that year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the herders' three signs and reports that the חכמים added a month because of them. This is the evidence behind the challenge to רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three signs describe the change from winter to spring that should mark אדר. The signs had not appeared, so the season was behind the calendar, and the חכמים added a month to bring them back in line. This suggests the months follow the seasons, which seems to contradict רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: And they made it a leap year

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא says the weather follows the counted months. The herders' story shows the חכמים adding a month to match the real season, which seems to say the opposite. The answer comes next.

phrases.english: One said:
If the early and the late crops sprout together –
this is Adar,
and if not – this is not Adar.
And one said:
If an ox in the morning would die in the snow,
and at midday lies down in the shade of a fig tree
rubbing off its skin –

phrases.aramaic: דֵּין הוּא אֲדָר, וְאִם לָאו – לֵית דֵּין אֲדָר.
phrases.english: this is Adar, and if not – this is not Adar.
And one said:
If there is a very strong east wind,
and the breath from your mouth goes out against it –
phrases.notes: Your warm breath beats the cold wind, a sign that spring is arriving.

phrases.aramaic: דֵּין הוּא אֲדָר, וְאִם לָאו – לֵית דֵּין אֲדָר.
phrases.english: this is Adar, and if not – this is not Adar.
And the Sages added a month to that year.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: אִם בַּכִּיר וְלַקִּישׁ כַּחֲדָא יֵינֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the story that step 23 introduced, completing the challenge to רב פפא
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that the months follow the seasons, against רב פפא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים added a month based on the herders' seasonal signs

steps.title: The חכמים relied on their own calculations, not on the herders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the חכמים used the herders' signs to decide the law. They used their own calendar calculations, and the herders' words just happened to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think the חכמים relied on cattle herders? No. The חכמים relied on their own calculations, and the herders' words just happened to agree with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the herders story from the last step. It says the story does not show that the herders' signs decided anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 seemed to show that nature's signs, like weather and crops, decide when a month is added. Here the גמרא says the חכמים decided based on their own calculations. The herders were only a side support. So the story cannot be used against רב פפא's idea that the weather follows the months.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a way of rejecting an idea)
To be supported, to happen to agree

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים set the calendar by their own calculations. Outside signs like the herders' words were at most a support, never the reason.

phrases.english: And can you really think that the Sages relied on herders?
Rather, the Sages relied on their own calculations,
and the cattle herders,
it is just that their words happened to be supported.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the herders brought in Step 24 against רב פפא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the herders story as a proof that nature's signs decide the calendar.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the חכמים relied on the herders. In fact they relied on their own calculations, and the herders only happened to agree.

steps.title: The משנה forbids יבום for the כהן גדול in every case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about the כהן גדול doing חליצה. It notes that the משנה forbids יבום for him whether the widow was only engaged or fully married to his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he does חליצה and others do חליצה with his wife. The משנה says this with no exceptions. It makes no difference whether she was widowed after betrothal or after full marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה about the כהן גדול and יבום. It points out that the rule has no exceptions, and this sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only that the כהן גדול does חליצה and never does יבום. The גמרא notices that the משנה does not tell apart a widow after betrothal (אירוסין) from a widow after full marriage (נישואין). Because the rule covers both, the גמרא will need a reason that works for both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Performs חליצה, the ceremony that frees a brother's widow from יבום
It teaches a rule with no exceptions
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: The new topic has nothing to do with adding a month. The גמרא has finished that discussion and is now back to the משנה's list of laws about the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: He performs חליצה, and others perform חליצה with his wife, etc.
It teaches this with no exceptions,
no difference whether she was widowed from betrothal
and no difference whether she was widowed from full marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹלֵץ וְחוֹלְצִין כּוּ׳. קָא פָּסֵיק וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, the כהן גדול never does יבום, whether his brother's widow was only betrothed or fully married.

steps.title: Why a widow from full marriage is clearly forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge. It grants that a widow from full marriage is forbidden to the כהן גדול, because both a positive command and a prohibition apply to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that a widow from full marriage is forbidden, because there is both a positive command and a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its question with "granted" (בשלמא). It first explains the easy case, to set up the hard case of a widow from betrothal, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman widowed after full marriage is no longer a virgin. So she breaks the positive command that the כהן גדול must marry a virgin, and also the prohibition against him marrying a widow. With two commands against it, the positive מצוה of יבום cannot override them. The hard question, still to come, is about a widow from betrothal who may still be a virgin.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this case makes sense (opens a question about a different case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This step prepares the main question. A positive מצוה like יבום usually can override a plain prohibition. So the גמרא must explain what blocks יבום when the widow is still a virgin from betrothal.

phrases.english: Granted, a widow from full marriage is forbidden,
since there is both a positive command and a prohibition —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:13 says he must marry a virgin, and ויקרא 21:14 forbids him to marry a widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts questioning the no-exceptions rule pointed out in Step 26, beginning with the easy case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the כהן גדול never does יבום, even with a widow from betrothal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow from full marriage breaks both a positive command and a prohibition, so the מצוה of יבום cannot override them. The question that follows will ask what forbids a widow from betrothal, who may break only one prohibition.
